nm2_modeling_method.answer: Multimodal Soft-Introspective Variational Autoencoder (mmSIVAE) with Mixture-of-Product-of-Experts (MOPOE) latent aggregation
nm2_modeling_method.reason: The paper clearly describes the modeling approach. The method extends Soft-Introspective VAE (SIVAE) to the multimodal setting and uses MOPOE for aggregating information from multiple modalities in the latent space. This is an adversarial training framework for VAEs that enables the encoder to distinguish between generated and real data.
nm2_modeling_method.supporting_text: We introduce a novel multimodal softintrospective VAE (mmSIVAE) for normative modeling across multiple neuroimaging modalities. SoftIntroVAE (SIVAE) (Daniel and Tamar, 2021) is a state-of-the-art framework for image generation and outof-distribution (OOD) detection, training a VAE adversarially to enable the encoder to distinguish between generated and real data. We extend SIVAE to handle multiple modalities... Second, we adopted the Mixtureof-Product-of-Experts (MOPOE) approach, combining the strengths of POE and MOE to aggregate multimodal information effectively in the latent space.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Latent-space Mahalanobis distance (D_ml); Feature-space Mahalanobis distance (D_mf); Latent Z-scores (Z_ml) for individual latent dimensions (|Z| > 1.96 or p < 0.05 as significant); Feature Z-scores (Z_mf) for regional deviations (|Z| < -1.96 for MRI, |Z| > 1.96 for amyloid/tau as abnormal after FDR correction)
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The paper uses multiple deviation metrics. Equation 16 defines latent Mahalanobis distance D_ml measuring deviation from healthy latent distribution. Equation 17 defines feature-space Mahalanobis distance D_mf based on reconstruction errors. Equations 18-19 define Z-scores for latent dimensions and features. Thresholds are explicitly stated: p<0.001 for outlier classification (Tabachnick et al. 2013), and |Z|>1.96 (p<0.05) for identifying significant latent dimensions. For regional features, |Z|<-1.96 for MRI atrophy and |Z|>1.96 for elevated amyloid/tau.

We identified 5 out of 15 latent dimensions (6,7,8,14 and 15) whose mean absolute Z ml > 1 . 96 ( p < 0 . 05 )... Z < -1.96 for MRI and Z > 1.96 for amyloid and tau

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Positive likelihood ratio = (proportion of disease subjects labeled as outliers) / (proportion of controls labeled as outliers) used to assess outlier detection performance; Earth Mover's Distance to quantify separation between control and disease deviation distributions; Pearson correlation with Steiger's Z-test to compare associations between deviations and neuropsychological composites (memory, executive, language, visual-spatial); linear regression adjusted for age and sex for associations with cognitive scores; Cohen's d effect size for pairwise group comparisons of regional deviations across CDR stages; FDR correction for multiple comparisons in regional analyses; Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with log-rank tests for CDR progression (shown in supplementary Figure/Table S4)
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: mmSIVAE with MOPOE aggregation achieved superior reconstruction of healthy controls, outperformed baseline methods in outlier detection (likelihood ratios up to 10.2), demonstrated strong associations with cognitive decline, and enabled interpretable mapping of latent deviations to brain regions associated with AD pathology.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The proposed mmSIVAE with MOPOE latent aggregation demonstrated the lowest reconstruction errors for both MRI and amyloid modalities across all brain regions compared to baseline models (SIVAE, mmVAE, VAE, mmJSD, JMVAE, MVTCAE). For outlier detection, latent Mahalanobis deviations achieved higher likelihood ratios (up to 10.2 for d=15 latent dimensions) compared to feature-space deviations (up to 3.34), with mmSIVAE+MOPOE consistently outperforming all baselines. Introspective VAE methods showed superior performance over vanilla VAE approaches. The Earth Mover's Distance between control and disease distributions was highest for mmSIVAE (34.043), indicating better separation. Latent deviations correlated significantly with cognitive decline: memory (r=-0.573), executive (r=-0.467), language (r=-0.421), and visual-spatial (r=-0.442), with significantly stronger correlations than mmVAE and VAE baselines (p<0.05 by Steiger's Z-test). Regional deviation patterns were consistent with known AD pathology, showing greatest MRI atrophy effects in temporal, parietal, and hippocampal regions, and elevated amyloid uptake in accumbens, precuneus, frontal, and temporal regions. Five latent dimensions (6,7,8,14,15) showed statistically significant deviations (|Z|>1.96) and were successfully mapped to interpretable regional abnormalities.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study demonstrated clinical validation across progressive AD stages (CDR 0, 0.5, ≥1) showing increasing effect sizes for regional deviations with disease severity. Kaplan-Meier survival analyses (Table S4) showed significant differences in CDR progression rates across deviation quartiles. The framework enables interpretation of latent space deviations by identifying significant latent dimensions and mapping them to feature-space abnormalities. Hamming distance was used to quantify within-group heterogeneity in abnormality patterns (Figure S2). The model was evaluated on both ADNI and external Knight ADRC datasets, suggesting generalizability.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is a preprint (dated December 13, 2024) and has not yet been peer-reviewed or published in a journal, hence no DOI. The paper extends previous work (Kumar, Payne, & Sotiras, 2023) on multimodal VAE normative modeling by incorporating the introspective VAE framework and MOPOE aggregation. There is some inconsistency in sample size reporting: main text states N=726 ADS total, but Table 1 shows only 360 (ADNI-ADS 231 + ADRC-ADS 129). The 248 training healthy controls are separate from the validation cohorts shown in Table S1 (ADNI-CU N=434, ADRC-CU N=301). The paper includes extensive theoretical analysis (Nash equilibrium proofs in Appendix A, MOPOE generalization proofs in Appendix B). Hyperparameters: β_rec=β_kl=1, β_neg=10, γ_r=10^-8, s=1/90, latent dimensions tested=[5,10,15,20] with d=15 showing best performance. The study used specific neuropsychological composite scores described in SM3, with some differences between ADNI and ADRC test batteries.
